source.statement: For rank-one Gaussian DSM with fixed sigma>0, unit v=u_i, linear Omega=Phi Theta, zero-mean initialization, a sufficiently small learning rate, and lambda_(D-1)>lambda_D>0, the mean error has rate O((1-2 eta rho_i)^t), with the same rho_i for i<D and a strictly larger rho_D. Near optimality, the trace scale of the SGD-step covariance is proportional to lambda_i.

assumptions: v is a unit eigenvector of Phi Phi^T
Phi is fixed and Phi Phi^T has a positive smallest eigenvalue
eta is small enough that all GD contraction factors are nonnegative

acceptance.symbolic_rate_certificate: all exact algebraic identities and strict inequalities pass
acceptance.exact_recurrence: closed form equals iterated population GD for every direction, t=0..12, in two predeclared rational spectra
acceptance.independent_checker: full Kronecker-Hessian eigenanalysis agrees with the rho formula and finite differences agree with the gradient
acceptance.sgd_covariance: Monte Carlo covariance-trace estimates have Pearson r > 0.999 with lambda and maximum relative error < 0.06
acceptance.training_simulation: population GD shows the predicted asymptotic contraction ordering; batch-one DSM SGD is executed and reported
acceptance.negative_control: the deliberately wrong rho_i=sigma^2 lambda_i rule is rejected
acceptance.exit_behavior: verifier exits nonzero if any acceptance item fails
